title: Heating and Cooling
seo_title: Grade 2 Science: Heating and Cooling Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe how heating and cooling change solids and liquids, such as melting and freezing; identify changes that can and cannot be undone; describe uses of water in each season. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Properties of Liquids and Solids)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 science worksheets on melting, freezing, heating and cooling and changes we can undo, with pictures. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Ice melts and water freezes. Some changes, like cooking an egg, cannot be undone.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heating and cooling can change solids and liquids.

  • Warmth melts ice, butter and chocolate.
  • Cold freezes water into ice.
  • Cooking an egg cannot be undone.
Example

What happens to ice in the sun?

it gets warm

Answer: it melts

Example

Can melted chocolate be solid again?

cool it down

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all changes can be undone.
  • Thinking water disappears when a puddle dries (it goes into the air).

faq.a: A solid turning into a liquid when it is heated, like ice turning into water.
A liquid turning into a solid when it gets very cold, like water turning into ice.

items.q: In Chloe's picture, snow changes into water. How could you change it back?
items.e: Melting and freezing can be undone.

items.q: What happens to a puddle on a hot sunny day?
c: It dries up as the water goes into the air.
items.e: Water evaporates.

items.q: In Benjamin's picture, an ice cube changes into water. Did heating or cooling cause it?
items.e: Melting comes from heating; freezing comes from cooling.

items.q: Kai observes: “Bread is toasted.” What caused this change?
items.e: Melting, cooking and baking come from heating. Freezing and hardening come from cooling.

items.q: What happens to an ice pop left on a table?
items.e: Room air is warmer than the freezer.

items.q: Nathan observes: “A crayon melts in a hot car.” Can this change be undone?
c: Yes, but only by adding salt.
No. It can never change back.
Yes. When it cools, it is hard again (in a new shape).
items.e: Melting and freezing can be undone.
